key_insight: An optical cavity enables fast, site-selective mid-circuit measurement and real-time feedforward in a neutral-atom array without strongly disturbing neighboring qubits.
engineering_relevance: This work pushes neutral-atom quantum hardware toward practical error correction and adaptive algorithms by shrinking the measurement-and-control cycle to under 100 microseconds.
method: Use local light shifts to detune non-target qubits from the cavity and protect their coherence.
Probe a selected qubit near resonance so its emission is Purcell-enhanced and efficiently collected.
Apply real-time feedforward to correct measurement-induced phases and drive adaptive state preparation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mid-circuit measurements of four qubits with sub-percent infidelity and less than 2% coherence loss on a fifth unmeasured qubit, with cycle time below 100 microseconds.
watch_item: The approach relies on precise cavity coupling, detuning control, and fast real-time feedback, which may be challenging to scale across larger arrays.
paper_title: Rapid Cavity-Based Mid-Circuit Measurement and Feedforward in a Neutral Atom Array
